newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australia nickel output, exports seen rising.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australia nickel output, exports seen rising.

text.p: Australian mine nickel production is expected to rise to 118,000 tonnes in 1996/97 to June 30 while exports are expected to rise by 14.5 percent to 141,000 tonnes from 123,000 a year earlier, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said.

In its June forecast, ABARE forecast production of 116,000 tonnes. The value of Australian nickel exports is projected to fall in 1996/97, despite a strong increase in export volumes, on the back of weaker prices and a strong Australian dollar, the government's chief commodities forecaster said.
ABARE, in its September quarter commodities bulletin, forecast export value to fall 1.8 percent to A$1.14 billion in the year to June 30, 1997, from A$1.16 billion in 1995/96.
"The decline (in earnings) represents forecast weaker prices in 1996/97, and an assumed stronger Australian dollar," it said.

The production forecast represents an 11 percent increase over 1995/96, compared with the previous projected increased of 14 percent after 1995/96 production forecasts were revised to 106,000 tonnes from 102,000 tonnes in the June outlook.

The bureau said the expected increase in nickel output in 1996/97 was due to increased output from WMC Ltd's Mount Keith operation and the underground mine at the Silver Swan deposit, both in Western Australia.
Silver Swan is jointly owned by unlisted Australian miner Mining Project Investors and Outokumpu Oy of Finland.
The bureau forecast world nickel prices to fall seven percent to average US$7,689 a tonne in calendar 1996, before recovering to about US$8,500 a tonne in 1997.
"However, there is some uncertainty attached to this price forecast because the nickel forecast can be extremely volatile," the bureau said.
"Given this volatility, it is estimated that there is a 75 percent probability of the final average price in 1997 being in the range of US$6,903 a tonne and US$9,120 a tonne."
